conversations --help.stdout:
Usage:
  flow conversations [options]
  flow conversations show <id> [--env production] [--json]

Lists the hosted agent's conversations, newest first: id, last message, channel, the agent version
behind its latest reply, contact, messages, and how many replies were graded wrong and unhelpful. show prints one conversation, one line per
message, and under each graded agent reply its label, the rule it was graded on, why, and the quoted
words; under an agent reply, its tool calls (name, time, ok or the error) and its delivery (queued,
sent, delivered, read or failed, with the channel's code) when Flow has them. show reads with
FLOW_KEY and, when Flow does not find the id with it, once more with FLOW_LIVE_KEY when set;
show --env production reads with FLOW_LIVE_KEY straight away. To fix bad replies:
flow conversations --grade wrong, then flow conversations show <id>.

Options:
  --env <name>             staging or production (default: production for a live key, else
                           staging); --environment works too
  --grade <label>          Only conversations with a reply graded wrong, unhelpful or good
  --contact <label>        Only this contact's conversations, by its label as listed: "Contact 9e35"
                           or 9e35 (read over as many pages as it takes)
  --since <when>           Only conversations with a message since then: 30m, 24h, 7d, or a time
                           such as 2026-10-29T09:00:00Z
  --limit <n>              At most this many conversations (default: 20, at most 1000), asked for 100 a
                           page over as many pages as it takes
  --json                   One JSON document on stdout: the server's (pages of conversations
                           merged into one), or { ok: false, error: { code, message, hint }, next }
                           when it did not work; every other line goes to stderr
  --cloud <url>            Flow's address (default: FLOW_FRAMEWORK_CLOUD, else https://flow.engineer/observe)
  --dotenv <path>          Read the environment from this file instead of the folder's .env
  --server <url>           Read over a hosted Flow MCP as you (flow mcp login), not with this
                           folder's keys (default: FLOW_MCP_SERVER)
  --agent <id|name>        With --server: which of your agents (default: your only one)
  -h, --help               Show this help

Reads with the agent's Flow key, FLOW_KEY (flow setup writes it into .env); production reads
(--env production, insights) read with the live Flow key FLOW_LIVE_KEY when it is set
(npx @flow-engineer/flow setup --live writes it), else FLOW_KEY. No key is ever printed. Each read prints how its
message text came, one line such as "Text: de-identified (...)"; --json keeps it as text_mode.
A 429 (60 reads a minute per key) is waited out, up to 30 s, and said on stderr; a read that hit a
network error or a 5xx is tried once more.
Exit status: 0 printed, 1 no key, or the server refused or could not be reached (its message and
hint are printed), 2 a wrong flag.

Keys (the environment wins over the agent's .env; errors name a key by its prefix and last 4 only):
  FLOW_KEY                  flow_test_... reads staging, flow_live_... staging and production:
                            flow conversations, flow issues, flow templates. flow setup makes a
                            flow_test_ one
  FLOW_LIVE_KEY             The agent's live Flow key, flow_live_...: production reads (flow
                            conversations --env production, flow conversations show of a
                            production one, flow insights) use it whenever it is set, with text
                            de-identified unless made with --content; npx @flow-engineer/flow setup --live makes it
                            (the workspace's owner), for 30 days, ending after 7 unused. It
                            reads, runs tests, writes traces and uses the model; it messages
                            customers or deploys live only after npx @flow-engineer/flow keys grant send|deploy
                            and the owner's one click
  FLOW_FRAMEWORK_CLOUD_KEY  The CI key, oci_...: flow test, flow show, flow deploy (every
                            subcommand), flow logs, flow cli publish|rollback|status
  npx @flow-engineer/flow setup writes both into .env (FLOW_KEY as a flow_test_ key), or copy them from your agent's Developers page on the dashboard (https://flow.engineer/dashboard).
Cloud (--cloud, else FLOW_FRAMEWORK_CLOUD): https://flow.engineer/observe (US, the default; /dashboard
  is the same) or https://flow.engineer/dashboard/in (an agent in the India cell).

logs --follow.stderr:
--until and --follow do not go together: --follow prints lines as they come.

Usage:
  flow logs [--env staging|production] [--since 1h] [--until <when>] [--severity <min>] [--grep <text>] [--limit <n>] [--follow] [--json]

  --env        Which (default: staging); --environment works too.
  --since      How far back: 30s, 15m, 1h (the default), 3d, at most 30d, or a time such as
               2026-11-03T09:00:00Z.
  --until      Up to when: a duration back from now (2h) or a time. Not with --follow.
  --severity   Only lines at this severity or above: DEFAULT, INFO, WARNING or ERROR. A DEFAULT line
               that is plainly an uncaught error (Error:, DOMException, a stack) counts as ERROR.
  --grep       Only lines that hold this text (any case) anywhere in the line as printed: a JSON
               line's every field, not only its message. Flow searches the fields' values; text
               with a quote or a brace ("step":"question", JSON as printed) is matched here
               instead, over every line of the window, which reads more pages.
  --limit      The most lines printed (default 10000, at most 100000): the newest are kept, and
               stderr says where the kept lines start and the --since/--until for the older ones.
  --follow     Keep printing new lines until Ctrl-C.
  --json       One JSON object per line on stdout: { time, severity, text }; nothing else goes there
               (a failure is one { ok: false, error, next } line).
  --dir, --cloud, FLOW_FRAMEWORK_CLOUD_KEY: as for flow deploy (flow deploy --help).
  --server     Read over a hosted Flow MCP as you (flow mcp login), not with the CI key (default:
               FLOW_MCP_SERVER); --agent <id|name> says which of your agents (default: your only one).

Flow sends only the lines that match --until, --grep and a --severity above ERROR (up to ERROR,
every line comes and is filtered here); an older Flow that does not filter gets them filtered
here, so the lines are the same either way. Flow keeps an agent's logs
for a while (30 days, older hosts 24 hours): when the lines start later than --since asked, stderr
says "Logs start at <time>: this Flow keeps <N> back". Flow answers in pages (500 lines); every
page up to --until (else now) is read before anything is printed, oldest line first. A stack
trace Cloud Run split into an entry per line prints as one: each line of it that starts with a
space ("    at ..."), at the same time from the same instance, joins the line before it, which
keeps the higher severity. With --grep, only the lines that match come, so a stack's "at" lines
show only when they match too.
